catalog_summary.by_form: skeletal ~121 (47%), displayed ~55 (21%), mixed skeletal-ring+condensed-substituent ~26 (10%), condensed ~22 (9%), structural/semi-condensed (FG templates + mechanism reactants) ~20 (8%), mechanism/reactive-intermediate ~13 (5%). Across 10 sources that carried data (NJC Topical was empty); ~257 catalogued structures.
catalog_summary.notable_gaps: Form coverage is lopsided by chapter: aromatic chapters (Arene notes/RP, Memory Sheet) are almost all skeletal ring drawings; the intro/summary chapters are almost all displayed; skeletal dominates overall. Only 1 of 12 sources (10 Intro to Organic) gives verbatim textbook DEFINITIONS of the representation forms, so form definitions rest largely on that one source. Stereochemistry is scarce relative to its importance: wedge/dash in only 4 sources, cis/trans in 3, and several chapters explicitly draw chiral/geometric species FLAT. Nitriles, esters, acyl chlorides, amides, radicals, delocalisation and polymers each appear in only a handful of sources. NJC 2019 Topical yielded no structures/conventions, and the mined JSON appears truncated at the 11th file (Ch21&22) so the nominal 12th source is not fully represented.

conventions_ranked.rule: Hydrogen is shown per form: DISPLAYED draws every C-H on its own bond; SKELETAL shows no C-H (any undrawn 4th bond on a carbon is an implied C-H); CONDENSED folds H into CH3/CH2 group labels. Hydrogen on heteroatoms (O-H, N-H, NH2, NH3+) is ALWAYS drawn, even in skeletal.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep. Verify skeletal always renders heteroatom H (OH/NH/NH2) and add an optional 'defining C-H' flag (aldehyde H, amino-acid alpha C-H) which several sources draw explicitly even in skeletal.

conventions_ranked.rule: Carboxylic acid label is inconsistent across and within sources: COOH, CO2H, and reversed HOOC-/HO2C- when the bond emerges from the left; the drawn/displayed form is -C(=O)-OH. A renderer must support all spellings, context-selectable.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Add an acid-label style option (COOH default, CO2H alt); auto-reverse to HOOC-/HO2C- when the group attaches from the left; render displayed acids as -C(=O)-OH.

conventions_ranked.rule: Carbon chain drawn horizontally left-to-right with the principal functional group at the RIGHT-hand end. Exception: amino acids are drawn NH2 on the left, COOH on the right.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep. Add the amino-acid exception (NH2 left / COOH right) and the memory-sheet rule that the amino-acid ionisation state matches reaction conditions (+H3N-...-COOH acidic vs H2N-...-COO- basic).

conventions_ranked.rule: DISPLAYED formulae use RIGHT-ANGLE (90 degrees) 'comb' geometry: horizontal C-C spine with strictly vertical C-H/substituent bonds, NOT a tetrahedral zig-zag. SKELETAL formulae use ~120 degrees tetrahedral zig-zag; sp2 C=C substituents splay ~120 degrees.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: HIGH: change displayed-form layout from 'natural tetrahedral/trigonal angles' to the orthogonal comb (horizontal spine, vertical H/substituent bonds). Keep 120-degree zig-zag for skeletal only.

conventions_ranked.rule: Benzene and all derivatives are drawn as a regular hexagon with an INSCRIBED CIRCLE (delocalised) as the house default; ring H implicit.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: HIGH: apply hexagon+inscribed-circle in ALL three forms; currently only the structural/condensed form is house-styled while displayed and skeletal rings are unstyled.

conventions_ranked.rule: Cycloalkanes/rings drawn as plain regular polygons with NO inscribed circle (this is how cyclohexane is distinguished from benzene); ring unsaturation added as a second parallel line on the affected edge (cyclohexene = 1, cyclohexadiene = 2). Substituents attach at a vertex.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: HIGH: implement ring rendering (regular polygons, vertex attachment, inner second line for ring C=C) and honour the plain-polygon-vs-circle distinction.

conventions_ranked.rule: Double bond = two parallel lines; triple bond = three parallel lines; roughly full length on chains (some sources draw the inner line shorter/inset for ring C=C), no large deliberate shortening.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep. Optionally draw the second line shorter/inset for ring double bonds to match RP style.

conventions_ranked.rule: C=O UP is the modal default (notes almost always put O above the carbonyl C), but orientation is PRAGMATIC: terminal aldehydes often draw =O to the side, esters sometimes down, ring ketones up, and the two -COOH of a symmetric diacid point in OPPOSITE directions; one summary source draws -COOH sideways with O-H hanging down.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep C=O-up as default but allow per-group orientation overrides: terminal aldehyde to the side, ester down, opposite directions for diacids.

conventions_ranked.rule: Formal charges as superscript +/- next to the atom; carbanion/carboxylate sometimes a CIRCLED minus (with lone-pair dots); partial charges as delta+/delta-; protonated amine as left-superscript +H3N-; complex ions in square brackets with an outside superscript charge; lone pairs as dot pairs.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Add charge glyphs (superscript +/-, circled-minus option, delta+/-, +H3N- left-superscript, [ ]^n complex ions) and lone-pair dot pairs.

conventions_ranked.rule: Atom labels sans-serif; digit counts as subscripts, charges/hybridisation as superscripts; structures monochrome black on white (colour only pedagogical: blue=answers, red=highlight/reagents/products). One source (RP Carbonyl) dissents with a serif face.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep Arial/sans-serif monochrome + subscripts. Optionally expose a serif toggle to match the Carbonyl RP source.

conventions_ranked.rule: Chlorine typeset 'Cl' with an ITALIC lowercase l everywhere (Cl2, HCl, AlCl3, CCl4, -Cl), a deliberate house quirk to distinguish l from digit 1; iodine uses a capital I; Br upright.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Cheap high-value fix: render the l in every chlorine label italic; keep I/Br upright.

conventions_ranked.rule: Reaction schemes: single straight arrow with reagent ABOVE and conditions BELOW; [O] for oxidation; equilibrium = double harpoon; reversible catalytic/aromatisation process = open double-headed arrow; resonance = double-headed straight arrow; crossed arrow / X = no reaction; memory sheet uses colour-coded paired forward/back arrows.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Separate scheme layer (out of single-structure scope): arrow primitives with above/below annotations, [O], and equilibrium/resonance/reversible/no-reaction variants.

conventions_ranked.rule: Ester drawn with an EXPLICIT carbonyl -C(=O)-O- (never condensed to -COO- in the drawing); contracted only inline as -CO2-/-OCO-.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Render esters as -C(=O)-O-R with explicit carbonyl in all drawn forms; reserve -COO-/-CO2- for inline condensed text only.

conventions_ranked.rule: Fused ring systems share an edge and may mix polygon sizes (hexagon+pentagon indane/indene, two fused hexagons naphthalene/decalin, hexagon+square benzocyclobutene, benzo fused to N-ring); 3-membered epoxide = triangle with O at apex.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Add fused-ring support: shared-edge polygon fusion, mixed ring sizes, heteroatom ring members, epoxide triangle.

conventions_ranked.rule: Condensed group labels are mirror-ordered by side: a group on the LEFT is written with its attaching atom last (H3C-, HO-, H2N-, O2N-, HOOC-); on the RIGHT with the attaching atom first (-CH3, -OH, -NH2, -NO2, -COOH), so the bonded atom always faces the bond.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Auto-reverse condensed group labels based on bond direction so the attaching atom touches the bond.

conventions_ranked.rule: Bold WEDGE = bond out of the plane (toward viewer); hashed/DASH = into the plane. Used for optical isomers as mirror-image PAIRS about a chiral C with four different groups, and for 3-D tetrahedral depictions. Definition stated verbatim in 10 Intro to Organic.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: HIGH: add wedge/dash bond rendering and optical-isomer mirror-pair layout; a formally defined A-level convention that is completely unhandled.

conventions_ranked.rule: Amide drawn -C(=O)-N(H)- with the N-H shown explicitly (also peptide bonds and anilides); not condensed to CONH2 in drawn form.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep (engine draws -C(=O)-NH2); ensure N-H is shown and support N-substituted (secondary) amides and peptide -C(=O)-NH-.

conventions_ranked.rule: On the ring the principal/first-named group sits at the TOP vertex; ortho (1,2) = adjacent vertex, para (1,4) = opposite/bottom vertex, 2,4,6-trisubstitution fills the two upper-side vertices + bottom. (10 Intro uses a flat-side hexagon variant with para drawn horizontally left/right.)
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Implement deterministic vertex placement (top / ortho-adjacent / para-opposite / 2,4,6) with pointy-top default; expose ring orientation.

conventions_ranked.rule: Curly arrows flow from electron-rich to electron-poor; FULL-headed arrow = electron pair (heterolysis), HALF/fishhook = single electron (homolysis/radical); lone pairs as dot pairs; arenium/Wheland intermediate = ring with broken inscribed circle + '+' (or circled +).
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Mechanism layer (separate feature): full/fishhook curly-arrow primitives, lone-pair dots, arenium broken-circle+plus rendering.

conventions_ranked.rule: Notes draw the aldehyde as a displayed -C(=O)-H cluster with H explicit (never text 'CHO' in the drawing); the RP arene bank instead condenses it to a 'CHO' label at the vertex. Genuine notes-vs-questionbank style conflict.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Keep explicit-H default (matches notes majority); add a 'CHO label' toggle for arene/question-bank style.

conventions_ranked.rule: Geometric isomerism shown by placing the two substituents on the SAME side (cis/Z) or OPPOSITE sides (trans/E) of a horizontal C=C; several sources draw geometry but never label E/Z; many notes omit it entirely.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Add cis/trans substituent placement across C=C (same-/opposite-side) for geometric isomers.

conventions_ranked.rule: Kekule ring (three alternating C=C, no circle) is used selectively: historical cyclohexa-1,3,5-triene, resonance canonical forms, NON-aromatic ring intermediates/products (arenium ions, Birch dienes, arene oxides), and as house style by some schools; the delocalised circle is the default everywhere else. Compilations can show both, even within one question.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Add a Kekule ring option for non-aromatic ring intermediates/resonance and school-specific styles; default stays circle.

conventions_ranked.rule: Free radical shown as a bold DOT on the atom (homolysis products of e.g. free-radical substitution).
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Low: add radical-dot glyph (needed only for free-radical substitution).

conventions_ranked.rule: Polymer repeat unit enclosed in square brackets with the two continuation bonds crossing the brackets and a subscript italic 'n'; an 'n' prefix on the monomer denotes polymerisation.
conventions_ranked.recommendation: Low: add repeat-unit brackets + crossing continuation bonds + subscript n.

form_definitions.consensus_definition: Full structural formula that shows every atom and every bond explicitly. Verbatim textbook definition only in '10 Intro to Organic Chemistry' ('shows ALL atoms and ALL bonds'); other sources use it without defining it, and 'Ch21&22 Summary' mislabels this fully-drawn form as its 'Structural Formula' column. House layout: right-angle/orthogonal comb (horizontal C-C spine, vertical C-H bonds), all H shown, C=O up by default, principal group at the right end.

Carbon chain drawn as a ~120-degree zig-zag; each line terminus/vertex is a carbon if no other atom symbol is written; C-H bonds are not shown, and any 'missing' bond on a 4-bonded carbon is an implied C-H; heteroatoms and their attached H are labelled; rings are polygons. Verbatim definition only in '10 Intro to Organic Chemistry'. It is the dominant catalogued form (~47%).

Shows the order/arrangement of atoms with groups written as text labels (CH3, CH2, OH, NH2, COOH); bonds largely not drawn out. '10 Intro to Organic Chemistry' defines the condensed structural formula as 'shows the order of arrangement of atoms; bonds are not displayed'. In practice sources also use a SEMI-condensed 'structural' hybrid (an explicit central C with right-angle bonds plus condensed end-groups) for functional-group templates and mechanism reactants.

Shows 3-D spatial arrangement: a bold WEDGE = bond out of the plane (toward viewer), a hashed/DASH = bond into the plane; used for optical isomers (a chiral C with four different groups) drawn as mirror pairs, and for tetrahedral 3-D depictions. Defined verbatim in '10 Intro to Organic Chemistry'.

refinement_backlog.item: House-style aromatic rings (hexagon + inscribed circle) in the displayed and skeletal forms, not only the condensed/structural form.
refinement_backlog.why: Benzene = hexagon + inscribed circle is the single most-supported drawing convention (8 sources) yet the engine leaves rings unstyled in 2 of its 3 forms.

refinement_backlog.item: Switch displayed-form bond geometry to the right-angle orthogonal 'comb' (horizontal spine + vertical H/substituent bonds); keep the 120-degree zig-zag only for skeletal.
refinement_backlog.why: 8 sources draw displayed formulae with right angles; the engine currently uses natural tetrahedral/trigonal angles, a direct mismatch with the house 'displayed' look.

refinement_backlog.item: Ring engine: render cycloalkanes/rings as plain regular polygons (no circle), attach substituents at vertices, draw ring C=C as a second inner edge line, pointy-top/vertex-up default.
refinement_backlog.why: 8 sources; the plain-polygon-vs-circle distinction is how students tell cyclohexane from benzene, and rings are currently unstyled in displayed and skeletal.

refinement_backlog.item: Wedge/dash stereochemistry plus optical-isomer mirror-pair layout.
refinement_backlog.why: A formally defined A-level convention (10 Intro) drawn in 4 sources; completely unhandled by the engine.

refinement_backlog.item: cis/trans geometry across C=C via same-side/opposite-side substituent placement.
refinement_backlog.why: 3 sources draw geometric isomers; examinable and unhandled.

refinement_backlog.item: Italic lowercase l in every chlorine label (Cl); keep I/Br upright.
refinement_backlog.why: Deliberate house quirk in 7 sources; a cheap typographic change with high recognisability value.

refinement_backlog.item: Carboxylic-acid label options (COOH default, CO2H alt) with automatic HOOC-/HO2C- reversal when attaching from the left; render displayed acids as -C(=O)-OH.
refinement_backlog.why: Acid spelling varies in all 10 data-bearing sources; a deterministic renderer must pick and reverse correctly.

refinement_backlog.item: Context-aware carbonyl orientation: keep C=O-up default but allow terminal aldehyde =O to the side, ester down, and opposite directions for the two -COOH of a diacid.
refinement_backlog.why: 8 sources show C=O direction is pragmatic; the engine hard-codes up.

refinement_backlog.item: Condensed-label mirror-ordering by bond side (H3C-/-CH3, HO-/-OH, H2N-/-NH2, O2N-/-NO2).
refinement_backlog.why: 5 sources; the bonded atom must face the bond for correct, professional-looking labels.

refinement_backlog.item: Fused/polycyclic ring support: shared-edge fusion, mixed polygon sizes, heteroatom ring members, epoxide triangle.
refinement_backlog.why: 5 sources (naphthalene, indane/indene, decalin, benzocyclobutene, tetrahydroquinoline, epoxides); unhandled.

refinement_backlog.item: Charge/ion glyphs: superscript +/-, circled-minus option for carbanion/carboxylate, delta+/- partial charges, left-superscript +H3N-, [ ]^n complex ions, lone-pair dot pairs.
refinement_backlog.why: 8 sources; needed for anions/cations, reactive intermediates, and condition-dependent acid-base forms.

refinement_backlog.item: Deterministic aromatic substituent placement (principal group top vertex, ortho = adjacent, para = opposite/bottom, 2,4,6 pattern).
refinement_backlog.why: 4 sources; substituted-arene rendering needs fixed, reproducible positions.

refinement_backlog.item: Draw esters with an explicit -C(=O)-O- carbonyl (not -COO-) in all drawn forms.
refinement_backlog.why: 5 sources; contraction to -COO-/-CO2- is reserved for inline text only.

refinement_backlog.item: Kekule ring option for non-aromatic ring intermediates/resonance forms and school-specific house styles.
refinement_backlog.why: 3 sources use Kekule selectively (arenium ions, Birch dienes, arene oxides, resonance canonical forms).

refinement_backlog.item: Aldehyde CHO-label toggle (arene/question-bank style) alongside the explicit -C(=O)-H default.
refinement_backlog.why: Notes draw -C(=O)-H (3 sources) but the RP arene bank labels it CHO, a genuine documented style conflict.

refinement_backlog.item: Reaction-scheme layer: single/equilibrium/reversible/resonance/no-reaction arrows with reagent-above and conditions-below, plus [O].
refinement_backlog.why: 7 sources render whole schemes; out of single-structure scope but needed for full-equation output.

refinement_backlog.item: Mechanism primitives: full-headed and fishhook curly arrows, lone pairs, arenium broken-circle+plus.
refinement_backlog.why: 4 sources; a large separate feature for mechanism drawing.

refinement_backlog.item: Free-radical bold-dot glyph.
refinement_backlog.why: 1 source (free-radical substitution); niche but currently impossible.

refinement_backlog.item: Polymer repeat-unit brackets with crossing continuation bonds + subscript n.
refinement_backlog.why: 1 source (polystyrene); niche addition-polymer need.

refinement_backlog.item: Optional serif label toggle.
refinement_backlog.why: One source (RP Carbonyl) uses a serif face against the sans-serif majority; low-impact parity option.
